title: Brigadeiro
subtitle: Brazilian chocolate fudge truffles rolled in chocolate sprinkles
excerpt: Rich, fudgy chocolate truffles made from condensed milk and cocoa, chilled and rolled in chocolate sprinkles. These are Brazil's most beloved birthday sweet, found at every children's party and family celebration. They take about 25 minutes to make and an hour to chill.
sourceNotes: Brigadeiro was created in Brazil in the 1940s and named after Brigadeiro Eduardo Gomes, a presidential candidate. The sweet was sold at campaign events to raise funds. It became embedded in Brazilian culture as the essential birthday party sweet and is now made in countless flavour variations across the country.

recipe.batchNotes: Easy to double or triple for a party. The mixture keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days before rolling.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the fudge mixture up to 5 days ahead and store covered in the fridge. Roll in sprinkles on the day.

content.text: This recipe makes 20 truffles and takes about 25 minutes of active cooking plus 1 hour of chilling. The mixture is just three ingredients cooked together in one pan, which makes it one of the most straightforward sweets you can make. The hardest part is stopping yourself eating the mixture straight from the pan.

Watch the mixture constantly as it cooks; it goes from loose to fudge-thick quickly and will burn on the bottom if you step away. You will know it is ready when you drag a spatula through the mixture and the gap takes a second to fill back in. Rub a little butter on your hands before rolling to stop the mixture sticking, and work quickly while the truffles are cold from the fridge.

items.prepNote: plus extra for your hands when rolling

content.text: Put the condensed milk, butter and 4 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder in a medium non-stick saucepan. Place over medium-low heat.

Stir constantly with a spatula or wooden spoon, making sure to scrape the base and sides of the pan. Cook for 10 to 15 minutes. The mixture will start thick, loosen slightly as it heats, then gradually thicken again.

Test for doneness by dragging the spatula through the mixture. When the gap holds for 2 to 3 seconds before slowly closing, the mixture is ready. It should pull away cleanly from the sides of the pan.

Pour the mixture onto a plate or shallow dish lightly greased with butter. Spread it out and leave to cool at room temperature for 10 minutes, then cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour until firm.
Pour chocolate sprinkles onto a plate. Rub a little butter on your hands. Scoop teaspoon-sized portions of the chilled mixture and roll into balls between your palms, working quickly.
Roll each ball in the chocolate sprinkles until well coated, then place in a paper case or on a tray. Refrigerate until ready to serve. Brigadeiros keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

attrs.symptom: Mixture is too soft to roll even after chilling
attrs.cause: The mixture was not cooked for long enough and still has too much moisture
attrs.fix: Return the mixture to the pan and cook for a further 5 minutes, stirring constantly. Then chill again for at least 1 hour.

attrs.cause: Heat was too high and the sugars in the condensed milk crystallised or the butter split
attrs.fix: Keep the heat at medium-low throughout and stir continuously. There is no rescue for a split batch; the mixture will have a dry, grainy texture and should be started again.

attrs.symptom: Truffles are sticking to hands and impossible to roll
attrs.cause: Mixture is too warm or hands are too warm
attrs.fix: Chill the mixture for longer, ideally 2 hours. Keep your hands cold by running them under cold water, then dry and butter them before each few rolls.

content.text: You will find brigadeiros at every birthday party in Brazil, piled on a platter in the middle of the table. They are made at home by children and adults alike, and are one of the first things many Brazilians learn to cook. Bakeries and sweet shops sell them in dozens of flavours, from pistachio to passion fruit, but the original chocolate version is still the one people reach for first.
